title: Teaching himself saxophone and gigging in Topeka
summary: Hearing Alphonso Trent's band in Oklahoma, he learns C-melody sax from a schoolmate, buys his first horn from Jenkins, and by the third year plays a weekly gig in Topeka.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: And I had... See, I didn't have no idea I had this talent for music. But in Oklahoma, in them early days, we heard so many good bands nad good Blues players, and guys played piano. Alphonso Trent's band used to come through there, and he had a great band. And I heard this, and that music was kind of in my ear. But I didn't discern(?) it until I started to fool around with it.

So making a long story short, another pupil in the school had a saxophone. I wasn't satisfied just playing this bugle horn. I didn't have sense enough maybe to move up to a trumpet. So I asked him would he... Now, this was

my first at the school. So I asked him would he show me a scale on the saxophone. So he did. And when he showed me that, I thought that was quite easy. The C, middle-C is your middle finger, the second finger on the top, and then B-natural change over, and then the rest of the notes you put one finger down at a time -- A, G, F, E, D, C.

I wasn't satisfied, though. I did that for a few days, maybe a week or so. So I asked him... I had sense enough to ask him to show me the chromatic scale. Because I figured I'd got so far in music then, that I know if I got the chromatic scale, I'd have all the notes. And the octave... You'd just raise the octave key to get the notes up higher. He showed me the chromatic scale. And Milt, I don't know the exact time, but as near as I can remember, in three or four months, I was playing that saxophone good enough to play for a little school dance. Just from ear. I had this ear. I picked up whatever songs they was playing there... And by it being a C-melody, there was no transposition involved. So I just played along with the piano. Whatever was on the piano, I could play on the...on the tenor. And I needed time(?) to play my little Jazz... I often wish I could hear some of that Jazz I was playing then; it wasn't nothin'. So...

Yeah, but I was involved with... And I found out I had this talent. So when I went home the next summer on the break of school, I got my mother to buy me my first horn. I'll never forget it. The name of the music store was Jenkins. And they sent off... And it looked like it took forever. It only took about two or three weeks, because I think Jenkins' head store was in Kansas City. So in about two weeks I had my horn. And I had been telling all of my friends around Muskogee, "Man, I can play the saxophone," but none of them didn't believe me.

So when I got that horn, my own new horn, boy, I was gone. That next year, when I went back to school with my own horn, I had it made. Because I could practice all I wanted to and... About the second, maybe it was the third year in school, I started giggin'... Because we had a little band in school, too. We had a guy who played trumpet, and we got together. But by about the third year in school, I started playing with a band in Topeka. I guess saxophone players were hard to find in them days! So I started playing with the band in Topeka. I just played maybe one gig a week. I think the most i made was five dollars. And we didn't know about no unions then...
